title: HRT myths, debunked
description: Hormone therapy carries decades of outdated fear, much of it traced to one widely misread study. Here's what current evidence actually says.
coverImageAlt: Woman researching the facts and myths around hormone therapy for perimenopause

slides.headline: "HRT causes cancer."
slides.body: For most women starting within ten years of menopause, the risk picture is far more favourable than early headlines suggested — and it varies by hormone type and personal history.

slides.headline: "It's only for severe hot flashes."
slides.body: It's also used for sleep, mood, joint aches, bone protection, and vaginal and urinary symptoms. Many women are surprised it can help with brain fog, too.

slides.headline: "You must stop after a few years."
slides.body: The old five-year rule of thumb is gone. Duration is now individualised — some women use it for a few years, others continue for a decade or more under supervision.

slides.headline: "It's unnatural."
slides.body: HRT replaces hormones your own body produced until recently, often at doses designed to be closer to natural levels than a typical menstrual cycle.

slides.headline: In India, these myths spread through family, not facts
slides.body: Many Indian women are discouraged from even asking about HRT by well-meaning relatives repeating decades-old fears. A real conversation with a gynaecologist is worth having before ruling it out.
